item.title: KASU unions suspend strike, insist on welfare demands
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo The Joint Action Committee (JAC) of Kaduna State University (KASU) has suspended its one-week warning strike following discussions with key stakeholders in the Kaduna State Government and the university management. The unions, however, said the suspension did not amount to abandoning their demands, insisting that outstanding welfare issues and agreements with the government must be fully addressed. JAC Chairperson, Sa’adiyya Mustapha, announced the suspension on Monday, explaining that the decision was taken to allow ongoing negotiations to continue and pave the way for an amicable resolution of the dispute. The committee comprises the Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU), the Non-Academic Staff Union of Educational and Associated Institutions (NASU) and the National Association of Academic Technologists (NAAT). Mustapha said the unions suspended the strike in the interest of the university after key stakeholders in the state government intervened and initiated discussions with them. “We have gone on a one-week strike and have now decided to suspend it, not because we are surrendering, but for the good of this university. “Several key stakeholders in this administration have made efforts to dialogue with us, and we have seen reason in those discussions. We have therefore decided to suspend the strike to show that we are willing to support the government and give dialogue a chance,” she said. She commended union members for their support and resilience during the industrial action, noting that the strike was intended to draw attention to their unresolved grievances. The JAC chairperson also reaffirmed the unions’ support for Governor Uba Sani, recalling previous salary-related challenges faced by university workers and the governor’s intervention in clearing outstanding payments. According to her, workers received half salaries in 2017, while their May 2023 salaries remained unpaid until the outstanding payments were presented to the governor and subsequently cleared after he assumed office. “Because of what he has done for us, we cannot say we are not in support of him. We support the governor and are solidly behind him. “However, what happened to JAC was what we were unhappy with, and that was why we decided to embark on the strike,” she said. Mustapha expressed optimism that the ongoing negotiations would produce positive results, urging the university management, governing council and state government to ensure fairness and equity in their dealings with staff. The industrial action followed a seven-day ultimatum issued by the three unions on November 2, 2026, to the Kaduna State Government and the university management over outstanding welfare demands and alleged failure to implement agreements reached with non-teaching staff unions. item.title: Beyoncé Becomes First Artiste To Reach 100 Grammy Nominations
item.description: American singer Beyoncé has become the first artiste in Grammy Awards history to receive 100 career nominations, extending her record as the most-nominated artiste in the award’s history. The milestone came with the announcement of the nominees for the 69th Annual Grammy Awards on Monday, November 16, 2026, following her nomination in the Best R&B Solo Performance category for her song ‘Morning Dew (Donk)’. The latest recognition takes Beyoncé’s nomination tally to 100, further widening her lead over other artistes, including her husband, rapper Jay-Z, who previously held the record alongside her. Beyoncé entered the Grammy nominations list in 2000 as a member of Destiny’s Child, earning nominations for ‘Bills, Bills, Bills’ in the Best R&B Song and Best R&B Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals categories. She subsequently built a record-breaking career across several genres, including R&B, pop, dance and electronic music, and country. This cover image released by Parkwood/Columbia/Sony shows “Cowboy Carter” by Beyoncé. Her latest nomination is for ‘Morning Dew (Donk)’, a previously unreleased recording from the sessions for her second studio album, ‘B’Day,’ released in 2006. The song was released on July 4, 2026, ahead of the album’s 20th anniversary, and later featured on its deluxe anniversary edition. Beyoncé and Pharrell Williams produced the track, which was written by the singer alongside Williams, The-Dream and Darius Dixon. Other nominees in the Best R&B Solo Performance category are Kehlani for ‘Out the Window’, Victoria Monét for ‘Let Me’, Jill Scott for ‘Pressha’ and Tems for ‘What You Need’. Beyond her nomination record, Beyoncé remains the most-awarded artiste in Grammy history, with 35 wins. A large Grammy award is seen outside the press room during the 62nd Annual Grammy Awards on January 26, 2020, in Los Angeles. (Photo by Frederic J. BROWN / AFP) She broke the record in 2023 after winning four awards at the 65th Grammy Awards, taking her total to 32 and surpassing the previous record of 31 held by classical conductor Georg Solti. She added three more awards in 2025. At the 67th Grammy Awards in 2025, Beyoncé also won Album of the Year and Best Country Album for ‘Cowboy Carter,’becoming the first Black woman to win the latter category. The 69th Grammy Awards ceremony is scheduled to hold on February 7, 2027, at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, California. item.title: Budget 2027: FG moves to cut overhead, orders MDAs to share facilities
item.description: …Targets spending on hotels, private venues for official meetings By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Federal Government has directed Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) to maximise the use of existing government-owned facilities instead of spending public funds on hotels and other privately owned venues for official meetings, as part of efforts to reduce overhead expenditure in the 2027 Budget. The move is part of a broader cost-saving initiative by the Federal Ministry of Finance, through its Efficiency Office (E-Office), to eliminate avoidable expenditure, improve the utilisation of public assets and ensure value for money in government operations. The Head of the Ministry’s Information and Public Relations Unit, Efe Ovuakporie, disclosed this in a statement issued in Abuja on Monday. She said the Efficiency Office was working towards establishing a coordinated system that would enable MDAs to identify and access available meeting and conference facilities across government institutions, thereby reducing the need to hire commercial venues for official engagements. According to her, a major component of the initiative is the compilation of a comprehensive directory of meeting facilities owned by MDAs nationwide. The directory, which will be published on the Federal Ministry of Finance’s website upon completion, is expected to provide government institutions with information on available facilities and make it easier for them to locate suitable venues. Ovuakporie explained that the arrangement would also enable MDAs with underutilised conference facilities to generate revenue by making them available to other government institutions, while reducing pressure on government overhead budgets. She said the initiative aligned with the Efficiency Office’s mandate to promote value for money, reduce overhead expenditure, monitor the utilisation of public assets and identify areas of waste across government institutions. In a related development, the Efficiency Office recently inspected shared government facilities across the five South-East states of Abia, Anambra, Ebonyi, Enugu and Imo to identify underutilised public infrastructure and opportunities for cost savings. The inspection covered selected Federal Secretariats, Federal Polytechnics, Federal Medical Centres and Federal Universities. According to the statement, the exercise assessed the condition, availability, utilisation and maintenance of the facilities, with particular attention to areas where improved management could enhance productivity and reduce unnecessary government spending. The inspection teams identified underutilised office spaces and facilities, deteriorating furniture, fittings and equipment, as well as inadequate maintenance of some offices and common areas. They also identified opportunities to improve the use of conference facilities and strengthen the organisation, storage and preservation of official records. item.title: Lagos PDP candidate promises tax exemption for teachers, doctors
item.description: By Cynthia Alo & Kafayat Kokumo The Lagos State governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Adedeji Doherty, has promised to exempt teachers and doctors from paying taxes if elected governor, saying his administration would deploy increased federal allocations to improve healthcare, education and residents’ welfare. Doherty made the pledge during an interview on Channels Television on Monday, where he also proposed a special tax card that would allow residents unable to afford the existing tax burden to pay N10,000 annually and enjoy subsidies on drugs and transportation. He said his proposed policy would ensure that increased revenue accruing to the state translated into direct benefits for residents. “When I am governor, I will definitely transfer these palliatives, these subsidies to my people. For instance, the doctors will not pay tax. For instance, the teachers will not pay tax. Those two people will not pay tax,” he said. Explaining the proposed tax card, Doherty said residents who could not afford to pay N50,000 annually would be allowed to pay N10,000 and benefit from subsidised medication and transportation. “Out of this N250 billion plus, I will transfer it into cards, whereby for those that cannot pay N50,000 per year in tax, I will create a card that you can pay N10,000 per year in tax, but you will get a subsidy in your drugs and you will get a subsidy in your transportation. “This is giving money back to the people of Lagos State because I have it. Mr President has given it to me and I am giving it to you,” he said. The PDP candidate also promised to introduce free education, arguing that the resources available to Lagos State would enable his administration to implement the policy. He justified his proposed tax exemption for doctors by citing an alleged shortage of medical personnel in the state, claiming that Lagos had about 3,000 doctors against an estimated requirement of 15,000. “We need close to about 15,000 doctors in Lagos State as we speak, but right now we have only about 3,000. So, if 3,000 doctors are not paying tax, please give me a break,” he said. Doherty also promised improved welfare packages, including comfortable accommodation, discounted food and car loans, to encourage medical professionals practising abroad to return to Lagos. “I want those experts in London, in America, in Germany, in Hungary. I want them to come back to Lagos and feel like they are even special. I will make them special, just like the teachers,” he said. He described teachers as critical to the future of the state, stressing the need to provide them with adequate training and support to prepare children for leadership and professional responsibilities. item.title: 2027: I want to deliver Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda in Lagos, says PDP’s Doherty
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Lagos State, Adedeji Doherty, has described President Bola Ahmed Tinubu as his National Leader, saying he is contesting against the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, to ensure that the President’s Renewed Hope agenda is properly implemented in the state. Doherty stated this on Monday during an interview on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily, where he explained why he was seeking to become Lagos governor despite his support for Tinubu and his administration’s national agenda. He said he supported Tinubu’s Renewed Hope agenda but disagreed with the way the APC-led government in Lagos State was implementing it. According to him, the failure to translate the President’s vision into reality in Lagos had contributed to political tensions, including alleged thuggery and the destruction of campaign materials. He said, “I am going against the APC governorship candidate in Lagos because they are not doing what they are supposed to do concerning the APC/Mr President’s agenda for the country. “When you do not crystallise the dream that is being made by your boss, then definitely all these fallouts of thuggery, removing of banners, tearing of posters and things like that, definitely is what is going to happen because you are trying to cover up your inadequacies in government.” The PDP candidate further described Tinubu as his National Leader, stressing that his support for the President and the Renewed Hope agenda did not extend to the way the agenda was being implemented in Lagos. He said, “Basically, you know? I’m going to support what I support fully, what my National Leader is doing. I support fully the Renewed Hope agenda, which is the agenda for the entire country, but I do not support the agenda as it is being materialised and crystallised in Lagos State.” The post 2027: I want to deliver Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda in Lagos, says PDP’s Doherty appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: UK actor Robert Pattinson to be new James Bond
item.description: British actor Robert Pattinson was Monday named as the new James Bond, stepping into the coveted role of the world’s most famous fictional spy. “Amazon MGM Studios have announced that Robert Pattinson will take on the iconic role of James Bond,” the studio said on the official 007.com website. Pattinson would succeed Daniel Craig as the super-suave MI6 agent, “ushering in a new era for one of cinema’s most celebrated characters”, the studios added. It will be the first Bond film since long-term Bond producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael Wilson stepped back and Amazon took creative control of the franchise, after acquiring the series’ parent company MGM. “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime,” Pattinson said. “To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement,” he added in a statement. Amazon MGM also announced that Oscar-nominated Canadian director Denis Villeneuve, behind such box-office hits as the “Dune” films, would be directing the next Bond movie from a script by “Peaky Blinders” creator Steven Knight. Knight said in May that Amazon has given him a licence to play with the legendary secret agent created by author Ian Fleming. “Bond has been bulletproof. People have been able to make mistakes and variations, and the character has survived,” Knight told Screen magazine at the Cannes Film Festival. “Because the core of it is like a diamond. You can’t touch it,” he added. Knight also told reporters that he has done research with “the SAS and even more secret outfits” for his reinvention of the next 007 movie. Pattinson, 40, started out in amateur dramatics before getting his break in “Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire” (2005) as Cedric Diggory, a champion for Hogwarts. But he rocketed to global fame for his part as brooding teen heartthrob in the romantic vampire saga “Twilight”. – ‘Extremely inventive’ – He was paid a reported $2 million for his lead in “Twilight” (2008), but by the time the saga wrapped up with the two parts of “Breaking Dawn” in 2011 and 2012, he was reportedly on $12.5 million plus 7.5 percent of the box office take. One of his first forays into edgier cinema came with 2012 drama “Cosmopolis”, in which he portrayed a self-destructive currency speculator as his life falls apart. The film was directed by legendary US auteur David Cronenberg, who described the actor as “extremely inventive”. He received critical acclaim after later switching to more independent films and was nominated for best actor at the Cannes festival in 2017 for neo-grindhouse crime caper “Good Time” by New York-based brothers Josh and Ben Safdie. In 2022, Amazon bought storied Hollywood studio MGM, which held distribution rights to Bond’s extensive back catalogue. But it was not until early 2025 that the company struck a deal with longtime Bond producers Wilson and Broccoli to obtain full creative control. item.title: INEC debunks claim of remote BVAS log-out before voting ends
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has dismissed as false and misleading a viral social media video alleging that the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) would be remotely logged out before the end of voting. The commission clarified that only the poll official operating the device has the authority to log in or log out of the BVAS during voter accreditation and the subsequent result upload process. INEC disclosed this in a statement posted on its official X platform on Monday, following the circulation of a video on Instagram alleging that voters would be logged out of the system before the conclusion of voting. Describing the claim as fabricated, the commission said each polling unit was assigned unique login credentials, which were issued to the Presiding Officer on the eve of an election. According to INEC, the credentials enable the poll official to log into the BVAS for voter accreditation on election day and subsequently upload the polling unit result sheet at the close of polls. “The claim that the BVAS can be remotely logged out before the conclusion of accreditation and voting is false,” the commission stated. It stressed that there was no provision for any external individual or authority to remotely log out the device. The commission also dismissed claims that election results uploaded offline could be lost, explaining that the IReV application had been upgraded to accommodate offline uploads. INEC said the enhancement followed experiences during the 2023 general election, when some poll officials were held hostage at their polling units because they could not upload results due to poor or non-existent network connectivity. It explained that the offline upload feature allows poll officials in areas with poor or no network coverage to upload polling unit result sheets in the presence of stakeholders at the polling unit. According to the commission, such results remain securely stored on the BVAS pending successful transmission to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV). ” As Poll Officials proceed from the polling unit to the Ward Collation Centre and the device reconnects to the internet, the result sheet is automatically transmitted to the IReV portal without requiring any further manual intervention,” it said. INEC assured Nigerians that the BVAS and IReV systems operate in accordance with established procedures designed to protect the integrity, transparency and credibility of the electoral process. The commission urged members of the public to disregard the video, refrain from creating or sharing unverified information and rely on its official communication channels for accurate information. It reaffirmed its commitment to transparency, accountability and the conduct of free, fair and credible elections. item.title: Plateau records 5,457 suspected diabetes cases in nine months
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS — The Plateau State Government has raised concerns over the growing burden of diabetes in the state, following the record of 5,457 suspected new cases between January and September 2026. The Commissioner for Health, Dr Nicholas Ba’amlong, disclosed this on Monday during a press briefing in Jos to commemorate the 2026 World Diabetes Day. Ba’amlong said the figure followed 5,546 suspected cases recorded in 2025, but clarified that the numbers represented suspected cases and not confirmed diagnoses. He said diabetes remained a major public health concern because many people were living with the condition without knowing their status. The commissioner also disclosed that findings from the 2024 nationwide Know Your Number, Control Your Number screening campaign showed that 14,359 people were screened in Plateau State, with 2,610, representing approximately 18 per cent, recording elevated blood glucose levels. He, however, cautioned that the findings did not represent the prevalence of diabetes in the state. According to him, the figures underscore the need to expand access to screening, diagnosis and treatment services. As part of activities marking this year’s World Diabetes Day, the Ministry of Health, in collaboration with the Plateau State chapters of the Diabetes Association of Nigeria and the Endocrine and Metabolic Society of Nigeria, conducted a free workplace screening exercise at the Joseph Gomwalk Secretariat Complex, Jos. Ba’amlong said the exercise targeted 1,000 civil servants and provided blood glucose and blood pressure checks, weight and body mass index assessments, health education, counselling and referrals for further medical attention where necessary. Speaking on government interventions, the commissioner said the administration of Governor Caleb Mutfwang was working towards extending diabetes education and screening services to underserved communities across the state’s 17 local government areas through existing primary healthcare facilities and community outreach programmes. He added that the government was exploring partnerships and appropriate medical technologies to improve access to diagnostic services, particularly at the primary healthcare level, while strengthening follow-up and referral systems for people with elevated blood glucose levels. “Screening is only the beginning. Early detection must lead to appropriate diagnosis and treatment,” he said. The commissioner urged residents, particularly those with a family history of diabetes, excess weight or high blood pressure, to check their blood glucose levels regularly and seek medical attention when necessary. He also advised residents to adopt healthy lifestyles through balanced diets, regular physical activity and weight management, while avoiding tobacco and limiting alcohol consumption. item.title: Ejiofor hails DSS DG over evacuation of Igbo youths from Wawa facility
item.description: By Nwabueze Okonkwo ONITSHA — Human rights lawyer, Sir Ifeanyi Ejiofor, has commended the Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS), Oluwatosin Adeola Ajayi, for reforms at the Wawa detention facility and the evacuation of a significant number of Igbo youths from the facility. Ejiofor also praised Ajayi for what he described as an end to the alleged arbitrary arrest and abduction of Igbo youths, which he claimed had become frequent under the previous leadership of the Service. The lawyer made the commendation in a statement on Monday titled, “Wawa Barracks: The horrifying testimonies of survivors of enforced disappearances under the Buhari regime — a time for Igbos to introspect”. He expressed concern over alleged abuses at the detention facility, including arbitrary arrests, torture, deprivation of medical attention and deaths, based on accounts he attributed to former detainees. According to him, the situation had at some point deteriorated to the extent that some individuals of Igbo extraction allegedly exploited security agencies to settle personal scores. He said the reported reforms under Ajayi had helped restore confidence and a measure of security in the South-East. “Happily, that dark chapter has been brought to an end, restoring confidence, peace and a measure of security in the South-East geopolitical zone,” he said. Ejiofor described the alleged experiences of detainees as disturbing, claiming that many Igbo youths had suffered under the previous DSS leadership. He, however, stressed that his criticism of alleged security abuses should not be interpreted as support for criminal activities by non-state actors operating in the region. ” No grievance, however genuine, confers a licence for criminality; equally, no allegation of criminality confers a licence for lawlessness by the State,” he said. The lawyer appealed to the DSS Director-General to facilitate the release of more detainees who, according to him, had no involvement in criminal activities and against whom there was no credible evidence of wrongdoing. He also urged the Service to withdraw charges allegedly founded on ethnic profiling, arguing that addressing the underlying causes of agitation was more important than sustaining what he described as prejudicial ethnic categorisation. Ejiofor further commended Ajayi for what he called commendable reforms within the Service, saying the intervention demonstrated the importance of professionalism and institutional changes in rebuilding public confidence. He called for an end to the use of propaganda as a security strategy, arguing that public trust could only be restored through justice, accountability and respect for citizens’ rights. The lawyer also urged the Igbo people to reflect on the crisis, warning against internal divisions and the exploitation of collective grievances by individuals seeking personal benefits. item.title: 2027: Shehu Buba inaugurates 1,000-member campaign council
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The governorship candidate of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) in Bauchi State, Senator Shehu Buba Umar, has inaugurated a 1,000-member campaign council ahead of the 2027 general elections, urging members to embrace unity, peaceful political engagement and issue-based campaigns. Buba, who represents Bauchi South Senatorial District in the National Assembly, inaugurated the council on Sunday, with members drawn from the 20 local government areas of the state. He described the inauguration as a major step towards strengthening the party’s grassroots mobilisation, coordinating its political activities and improving its chances in the 2027 governorship election. The senator said the council comprised experienced party stakeholders and directors representing the various senatorial districts and local government areas, with the responsibility of developing strategies and coordinating campaign activities. He urged members to set aside personal differences and work collectively towards the party’s victory, stressing that political disagreements should be resolved through dialogue, persuasion and mutual understanding. Buba warned against violence, slander and character assassination, insisting that electoral victory could only be achieved through constructive engagement with voters and the presentation of credible alternatives. He said his ambition to govern Bauchi State was driven by the desire to address what he described as challenges of misgovernance and redirect the state towards sustainable development and prosperity. According to him, his development agenda will focus on economic stability and growth, improved security, urban and rural infrastructure, people-oriented reforms and the general welfare of residents. The PRP candidate also emphasised the importance of grassroots mobilisation, adequate electoral preparation and voter education, particularly on the need for voters to protect their votes after casting their ballots. He noted that effective governance would require cooperation between the executive and legislative arms of government, expressing the need for the PRP to secure representation in the State House of Assembly and National Assembly to facilitate the implementation of its manifesto. Describing the 2027 contest as challenging, Buba charged members of the campaign council to develop a workable programme and adopt strategies capable of securing victory for the party. He urged them to take the campaign to communities, wards and polling units, listen to residents’ concerns and communicate the party’s programmes and policies to the electorate. He further insisted that the PRP’s campaign should be guided by respect for voters and issue-based engagement rather than unnecessary attacks on political opponents. Expressing confidence in the party’s chances, Buba identified unity, commitment, hard work and popular support as critical factors for victory. item.title: 2027: Tinubu, Oborevwori assured of victory in Delta — Olejeme
item.description: By Precious Enaike The Zonal Director, South-South Election Planning, Coordination, Monitoring and Mobilisation of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Dr. Ngozi Olejeme, has expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu, Delta State Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and other APC candidates will win the 2027 general elections. Olejeme attributed her optimism to what she described as the growing strength of grassroots mobilisation within the party’s campaign structure, particularly in Oshimili South Local Government Area of Delta State. She spoke at the Oshimili South Arcade, Asaba, where she joined other party leaders in welcoming Oborevwori, his deputy, Sir Monday Onyeme, former Governor Ifeanyi Okowa and other members of the State Campaign Council to the local government. The former boss of the Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF) assured the governor that her council was prepared to mobilise support for all APC candidates in the area. Addressing party supporters, traders, youths and other residents at the rally, Olejeme expressed confidence that sustained grassroots engagement would translate into overwhelming electoral support for the APC. She said, “My Governor, we are here to tell you that Tinubu has already won. All APC candidates have already won. Mr. Governor, Oshimili South is the capital of government, and we trust and believe in you. “Based on the work we have done so far at the grassroots, I can assure you that we have already delivered President Tinubu and you, our confirmed Governor.” Olejeme, however, urged residents and party supporters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), stressing that grassroots mobilisation must be backed by active participation in the electoral process. “I have only one request to make: Go and make sure you collect your PVC. Your PVC is what will give us this victory. Collect your PVC; it is very important because we are already set for victory. We have reached our promised land, and your PVC is of immense importance at this point,” she said. She described Oborevwori as a performing governor who had exceeded expectations, while applauding Tinubu for what she called his achievements in office. Olejeme urged Nigerians to give the President another mandate in 2027, arguing that his performance deserved a second term. “Our Governor has performed very well. Governor Oborevwori is the best in Africa. President Tinubu has done so much that the people are not talking about. For the good work he has done, we have to give him more work to do by re-electing him in the 2027 general election,” she said. item.title: No casualty as gas explosion rocks Lagos NNPC station, spreads to school
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni A gas explosion on Sunday rocked a Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) filling station at Savannah Bus Stop, Command, Ejigbo, Lagos State, triggering a fire that spread to the adjoining Saint Lawrence Greater Height School. No casualty was recorded in the incident, which occurred at about 1pm, as the school was closed for the weekend. The Controller-General of the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, Margaret Adeseye, who confirmed the incident, said the fire was successfully contained through the prompt intervention of firefighters. Adeseye said the agency received a distress call at 12:50pm and arrived at the scene at 1:13pm. She disclosed that firefighters from Ejigbo, Ikeja and Bolade fire stations were deployed to the scene to combat the fire, prevent further damage and bring the situation under control. According to her, the intensity of the explosion caused the fire to spread rapidly to the adjoining school, affecting parts of its premises. She, however, said the firefighters prevented the fire from spreading to other sections of the school. “No casualty was recorded in the incident,” Adeseye stated. She added that preliminary investigations into the cause of the explosion were ongoing. item.title: Showunmi urges Ribadu to sanction politicians threatening security
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Convener of The Alternative Movement, Otunba Segun Showunmi, has urged the National Security Adviser, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, to establish clear standards for political conduct and ensure that politicians whose actions threaten Nigeria’s peace and security are held accountable, irrespective of their status or political affiliation. Showunmi made the call in an open letter to Ribadu, expressing concern over what he described as the growing toxicity of political engagement, reckless public communication and the increasing use of inflammatory rhetoric by politicians, their supporters and other influential individuals. In the letter, titled, “An Open Letter to the National Security Adviser: On the Urgent Need to Establish Firm Boundaries for Political Conduct and Hold Those Who Threaten National Security Accountable,” he warned that Nigeria’s already precarious security situation could worsen if political actors continued to exploit sensitive national issues for partisan advantage. The letter was also copied to President Bola Tinubu; the Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (rtd.); the President’s Special Adviser on Homeland Security, Major General Adeyinka A. Famadewa (rtd.); the Inspector-General of Police, Mr Olatunji Rilwan Disu; the Director-General of the Department of State Services, Mr Oluwatosin Ajayi; and the Minister of State for Defence, Alhaji Bello Muhammad Matawalle. Showunmi argued that political competition, personal ambition and partisan disagreements should not become additional threats to national stability. He noted that Nigeria was already grappling with multiple security challenges requiring vigilance, effective intelligence gathering, institutional coordination and responsible leadership. He urged political actors to recognise the far-reaching consequences of their words and actions. “There is a difference between robust political engagement and conduct that deliberately or recklessly threatens public peace. There is a difference between criticising government and deliberately inciting citizens against one another,” he stated. He cautioned against the abuse of freedom of expression to promote hostility, circulate inflammatory narratives and undermine national cohesion. According to him, the apparent normalisation of provocative statements, ethnic and religious insinuations, threats and inflammatory public performances had become a worrying development requiring urgent institutional attention. “Some individuals seem to believe that because they are politicians, party loyalists, public commentators or influential supporters of powerful political interests, they can say virtually anything, mobilise others irresponsibly and walk away without consequences. That assumption must be firmly challenged,” he said. item.title: Reps give NSCDC CG 24 hours over ₦2bn transactions, extortion allegations
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives Committee on Solid Minerals has given the Commandant-General of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) 24 hours to appear before it over allegations of financial impropriety, extortion, unlawful arrests and human rights violations involving the Mining Marshals. The committee is also seeking explanations over the alleged killing of a serving NSCDC officer, Deputy Superintendent Agada Levi Agada, reportedly by fellow officers while on duty at a mining site. The ultimatum followed a motion moved by Hon. Ali Amburura, representing Sokoto State, and seconded by Hon. Majidi from Katsina State during an investigative hearing into the activities, funding and operations of the Mining Marshals. The committee’s Chairman, Hon. Gaza Gbefwi, said the investigation was prompted by allegations of abuse of power, extortion, unlawful detention of licensed mining operators and financial irregularities within the special security unit established to combat illegal mining. Gbefwi said the lawmakers were particularly concerned about an alleged transaction of over ₦2bn linked to the bank account of a former state commander, suspected compromise among Mining Marshals personnel across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, as well as questions surrounding vehicle procurement and the unit’s sources of funding. He said the investigation was being conducted in accordance with the National Assembly’s constitutional oversight powers under Sections 88 and 89 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended. The lawmaker recalled that more than 2,200 Mining Marshals were inaugurated in March 2024 to strengthen the fight against illegal mining, protect the country’s mineral resources and improve security at mining locations. He also called for the protection of the family of the deceased officer and other witnesses, alleging that some had been subjected to threats and intimidation. According to him, Agada left behind a widow and two children aged 10 and seven. Gbefwi expressed condolences to the deceased officer’s family and assured them that their petition would be forwarded to the appropriate authorities for necessary action. He also requested an executive summary of the family’s submissions to assist the committee in documenting the allegations and determining appropriate interventions. Meanwhile, the Director of Communications at Stone Rockers Nigeria Limited, Rachel Ogbonna, accused the Mining Marshals of subjecting licensed mining operators to arbitrary arrests, prolonged detention and harassment. Ogbonna told the committee that the company’s quarry site had remained sealed for over one year despite its possession of valid mining licences and other relevant operational documents. She alleged that 12 employees of the company were arrested and taken to an NSCDC detention facility along Airport Road. item.title: Belgium’s Lukaku retires from international football
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Romelu Lukaku has retired from international football, bringing his 16-year Belgium career to a close as the country’s all-time leading men’s goalscorer. The 33-year-old striker scored 94 goals in 135 appearances for the Red Devils. He made his international debut in 2010 and represented Belgium at four World Cups and three European Championships. In a statement on social media, Lukaku said: “These 16 years I gave all I had for the national team. I went through every emotion possible. I played with amazing teammates that I will always be grateful for. “I want to thank them all. I want to thank all the coaches as well for pushing and trusting me to help the team. It was a nice ride, and I enjoyed every single moment.” He added: “To the Belgium fans, thank you for the support you gave our team. I am proud to have represented my country in 4 World Cups and 3 European Championships. “I will never forget those moments. I’m at peace with my decision to stop here. It was amazing. It was enjoyable I’m grateful. Thank you.” Lukaku is the fifth-highest men’s international goalscorer of all time, behind Sunil Chhetri, Ali Daei, Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, who leads the list with 146 goals. He scored eight goals across four World Cups, including during Belgium’s run to the quarter-finals at this summer’s tournament, and six goals at three European Championships. In 2023, he scored 14 times in eight Euro 2024 qualifying appearances, setting a record for goals in a single European Championship qualifying campaign. item.title: [PHOTOS] Nigeria Re-Elected To Council Of International Telecommunication Union
item.description: Nigeria has been re-elected to the Council of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) at the ongoing conference in Doha, Qatar. With this development, Nigeria retains its seat on the council for the term 2027-2030. As part of Nigeria’s campaign for re-election, the Ambassador to Qatar Mahmood Yakubu (right) had a bilateral meeting with Mr. Jijun Xiong, China’s Vice Minister of Industry and Information Technology and Leader of the Chinese delegation to the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) conference (Doha 2026). Established in 1865 with headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland, the ITU is the United Nations specialised agency for information and communication technologies (ICTs). It brings together 194 member states and over 1,000 sector members, which include companies, universities and international organisations. Nigeria became a member in 1961. Nigeria’s participation was coordinated by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu. The Nigerian delegation was led by the Minister of Communication, Innovation and Digital Economy, Bosun Tijani. With this development, Nigeria retains its seat on the council for the term 2027-2030. Nigeria’s Ambassador to the State of Qatar, Mahmood Yakubu, served as the Deputy Head of Delegation, supported by the Executive Vice Chairman of the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC), Aminu Maida; Nigeria’s Permanent Mission to Geneva, led by Innocent Imejuo; officials of the Ministry of Communication (NCC) and staff of the Nigerian Embassy in Doha. item.title: British Singer Raye Tops 2027 Grammys With 11 Nominations
item.description: Soulful British singer-songwriter Raye on Monday topped the Grammy nominations with 11, and Spanish superstar Rosalía earned nine in a strong showing for female artists across the board. Women have historically been underrepresented at the Grammy Awards held by the Recording Academy, whose 69th annual gala will take place on February 7 in Los Angeles. Spanish singer-songwriter and actress Rosalia attends the 27th Annual Latin Grammy Awards at the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas, Nevada on November 12, 2026. Photo by CHRIS DELMAS / AFP But recent years have seen women dominate both the industry and the trophies list. Raye’s whopping 11 nominations included the three most prestigious, recognizing best album, best song, and best record for her jazz-inflected blend of pop and R&B. She was also recognized for her songwriting for fellow artists with a nomination for the relatively new best songwriter category. Rosalia’s nine nominations follow a banner night at last week’s Latin Grammys, where her sweeping, avant-garde classical pop album “Lux” reigned supreme. First-time nominee Ella Langley, the crooner behind the ubiquitous smash hit “Choosin’ Texas,” will enter the evening with seven shots at Grammys gold, as will fellow country star Miranda Lambert, who co-wrote that hit and notably scooped a nomination for producer of the year. Pop-rock phenom Olivia Rodrigo also earned seven nods, as did the multifaceted musician Phoebe Bridgers, who released her third solo studio album “Lost Weekend” to widespread critical acclaim. First-timers make waves Leon Thomas and Olivia Dean — the English singer behind the smash “Man I Need” — earned six nods as did perennial Academy favorite Bruno Mars. Taylor Swift predictably will be a threat in the top categories for her album “The Life of a Showgirl” as well as the song she penned for the latest film in the “Toy Story” franchise. She has five chances at winning. But for all the heavyweight glory, it also proved a strong Grammys cycle for first-time nominees. New York indie rockers Geese capped a breakout year with their first-ever nominations, garnering five. Langley is a strong favorite for the Best New Artist category, but a crop of performers including Geese as well as brash electropop star Slayyyter and Canadian rock duo Angine de Poitrine could pull upsets. The new blood will be joined by stalwarts of the trade who earned nominations including Madonna, Paul McCartney, Bruce Springsteen and The Rolling Stones. The 2027 line-up features 100 competitive categories. The Grammy Awards will air on the US network ABC and stream on Disney+ and Hulu — the first time in half-a-century that the ceremony won’t be broadcast by CBS.
